# NASA mobile launcher source

`MobileLauncher-source.glb` is the unmodified **Mobile Launcher (assembled)**
model, by NASA / Samuel H. Neblett, from NASA's [3D resource page](https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/mobile-launcher/).
It is included so the model can be inspected and edited again from the original.
The source was downloaded from the [pinned NASA repository revision](https://github.com/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources/tree/11ebb4ee043715aefbba6aeec8a61746fad67fa7/3D%20Models/Mobile%20Launcher).

- SHA-256: `411ad36727a4290123431e77ca7a4622dcd534e2e76eb1134dc19fc07dd5be65`
- NASA's [3D Resources repository](https://github.com/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources) describes its assets as free and without copyright. Follow [NASA's media usage guidance](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/); credit NASA and do not imply endorsement.
- NASA's model page does not specify an exact vehicle configuration, original scale, or survey accuracy. Its text matches NASA's [2018 description](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/groundsystems/2018/03/21/last-of-the-big-swing-arm-umbilicals-installed-on-mobile-launcher/) of the SLS mobile launcher; the broad silhouette also resembles NASA's [ML1 photographs](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mobile_Launcher_1_(ML-1)_Rolls_to_Launch_Pad_39B_for_Artemis_ll_(KSC-20230817-PH-KLS01_0140).jpg). This is a simplified visual reference, not a verified current as-built model.
- The model contains Draco-compressed geometry and packed image textures; import it using software with Draco support. Its animated node has a 0.01 scale, so raw mesh coordinates are not already in meters.

This source archive alone does not add the launcher to the game.
